ASSUMPTIONS, EVERY SETTING WHOSE REASON SAYS IT IS ASSUMED
weather.inside_celsius = 20 celsius; reason: assumed design day
weather.outside_celsius = 0 celsius; reason: assumed design day
weather.sun_watt_per_square_metre = 500 w_per_m2; reason: assumed clear-sky peak; the solver applies it to every side
finish.mean_reflectance = 0.5 ratio; reason: assumed mid-grey interior; Jim's wall finish gives it
finish.sky_angle_degrees = 65 degree; reason: assumed open sky; the site gives it
doors.offset_mm = 0 mm; reason: assumed: the west end of the north wall; which end the door is at is open
joists.spacing_mm = 406 mm; reason: assumed: 16 in on centre
ledgers.member_width_mm = not given mm; reason: assumed: a ledger cut from the joist stock, fastened to the wall's inside face; the fastening is not
checked
ledgers.member_depth_mm = not given mm; reason: assumed: a ledger cut from the joist stock, as deep as the joists it carries
header.plies = 2 count; reason: assumed: two plies side by side, 3-1/2 in of LVL or 3 in of 2x lumber, fit inside the SIP's 3-5/8 in core
(sip.prs610_core_thickness)
roof_loads.roof_dead_load_psf = 15 psf; reason: assumed: 15 psf, the roof dead load Boise's roof-only header look-up assumes, research row
gl.hdr.vl_lookup_roof_only; the roof build-up gives it
roof_loads.deflection_limit_ratio = 240 ratio; reason: assumed: span over 240, the live-load deflection limit of Boise's header tables, research row
gl.hdr.vl_limits, applied to the whole load
roof_loads.roof_bears_on = south, north compass_sides; reason: assumed: the roof's 8 ft south hangover can only be carried by members running
north-south across the south wall, so the roof bears on the south and north walls
